meta.studentProfile: one-to-one adult or teen English learner
meta.communicativeGoal: Talk about friendships, secrets, and personal experiences using infinitive and gerund forms

hero.title: Luca: A Story of Friendship and Discovery
hero.subtitle: Learn about Luca and his friends — and practise using infinitives and gerunds in English.

controls.instruction: Say the first word that comes to mind for each word. Click a word after you discuss it.
Move each statement to Agree, Not sure, or Disagree. Be ready to explain your choice.

items.text: It is important to keep secrets from your parents sometimes.
Being different from other people is hard.
Friends can change your life completely.
Trying new things is more exciting than scary.
Parents always know what is best for their children.
You should always tell the truth to your best friend.
It is better to have one true friend than many friends.
You need to be brave to make new friends.

controls.title: Time to Read!
paragraphs: Luca is a young sea monster. He lives under the water near the Italian coast. His family tells him not to go to the surface. But Luca is very curious about the world above. He dreams of seeing the land and the sky.

One day, Luca meets Alberto. Alberto is also a sea monster. But he is different. He is not afraid of the surface. He enjoys living on land. He shows Luca how to walk like a human. Luca starts to enjoy his new life too.
The two friends want to buy a Vespa. They dream of travelling around the world. But they need money first. They decide to enter a race in Portorosso. The race prize is money for a Vespa.
In Portorosso, Luca and Alberto meet Giulia. She is a brave and friendly girl. She teaches them many things about the town. Luca learns about true friendship. But he is afraid to show his true self.
At the end, Luca decides to stop hiding. He shows everyone he is a sea monster. His friends accept him. Luca understands that being different is okay. True friends love you for who you are.

cards.title: Gerund: Verb + -ing
cards.body: We use the gerund after these verbs: enjoy, like, love, hate, finish, stop, keep, suggest. We also use it after prepositions (at, of, about, for, in).
examples: Luca enjoys swimming in the sea.
Alberto is good at making pasta.

cards.title: Infinitive: To + Verb
cards.body: We use the infinitive after these verbs: want, need, decide, plan, hope, learn, promise. We also use it after adjectives.
examples: Luca wants to explore the surface.
He decided to hide his secret.
It is scary to be different.

cards.title: Like / Love / Hate + Gerund or Infinitive
cards.body: After like, love, and hate, you can use the gerund or the infinitive. The meaning is the same. Both forms are correct.
examples: Luca likes swimming. = Luca likes to swim.
They love racing. = They love to race.

lessonFlow: Start with the Warm Up: show each word and ask the student to say the first association. Keep it fast and fun.
Move to Lead-In: the student sorts opinion statements. Ask follow-up questions about their choices.
Target Vocabulary: work through the definition match together. Then complete the gap-fill for practice.
Reading: give the student time to read silently. Then answer the quiz. Discuss one question in more detail.
Grammar: present the rule cards on infinitive vs. gerund. Use the completeRule and chooseCorrect activities to check understanding.
Grammar Practice: the student completes controlledInputPractice and dropdownChoicePractice. Correct any mistakes together.
Speaking: use the speaking questions for a natural conversation. Optionally do Translation Time for Russian-speaking students.
Resources: add any links or notes. Review what the student learned today.
adaptationNotes: For weaker students: focus only on the most common verb patterns (like + -ing, want + to). Skip the verbs that take both forms card.
For stronger students: add more verbs that take both forms (remember, forget, try) and discuss how the meaning changes.
If the student has not seen the film: give a quick 2-minute summary before the reading section.
For teens: use the speaking questions to talk about their own friendships and secrets.
For adults: adapt speaking questions to talk about childhood memories and friendships over time.
